Emma Patel: quick accessibility callout on the Quickstart sample-project picker in the first-run flow — NVDA reads the project card title twice and the primary CTA is announced after the secondary. cc @Josh Kim :eyes: Josh Kim: I saw that in the last usability pass. repro steps? which screen reader + browser? Emma Patel: NVDA + Firefox. Steps: open console -> start quickstart -> sample picker appears -> NVDA reads "Sample Projects, group" then reads the card title twice, then says "link" for the CTA. Also keyboard users land on the card container, not directly on the action button. Lia Morales: sounds like DOM order + aria roles. If card is a focusable region with inner link/button, screen reader may announce container then child. We should either make the card non-focusable and expose a single button, or make the container a `role="button"` with `aria-label` describing the action. Sam O'Neill: +1. Preference: keep keyboard press on card to open the sample import modal. So container should be keyboard focusable, but aria should not duplicate the title. Example: `role="button" aria-label="Open sample: Customer Support Assistant"` and then hide inner CTA from AT using `aria-hidden="true"` maybe. Josh Kim: low-code example — can we avoid `aria-hidden` on interactive elements? Might break keyboard users. Instead, collapse visual button into the container and keep only one focus target. We can keep inner action for mouse only with `tabindex="-1"`. Lia Morales: agreed. Proposed markup snippet: ```html

Sales Assistant

3 templates · 2 datasets

``` Emma Patel: also color contrast: the tag pill text (light-gray on soft-gray) is failing AA at 14px. Current colors: #7f8a9a on #f2f4f6 — contrast 3.8:1. Need >=4.5:1 for body. Options: darken text to #5b6a7a or increase weight/size. Sam O'Neill: if we bump weight it's OK for designs, but may shift layout. My vote: darken to #596878 and keep 14px. Saves layout churn. Josh Kim: one more: focus ring order — when modal opens from sample, focus goes to modal close button, but the first interactive element should be the top-level primary action (Import). Let's ensure `focus-trap` sets initialFocus to `.import-primary` in the modal code. Emma Patel: microcopy: change CTA label from "Use sample" -> "Import sample" in the modal. In the picker it can remain "Preview" when hovering. Also update sr-only label to include dataset count for screen readers. aria-qa-bot: automated note: accessibility checklist item added: `picker-card-single-focus-target`, `picker-contrast-pills`, `modal-initial-focus`. Tests queued: keyboard-only nav + NVDA smoke. ETA: 2 business days. design-bot: Figma frames updated: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd/quickstart-onboarding?node-id=432%3A21 — updated token for pill color to `--muted-text-contrast` (#596878). Please review frame "Sample Picker / a11y" Lia Morales: acceptance criteria I'd suggest: - NVDA reads single line: "Sales Assistant, 3 templates, 2 datasets, button Import sample" - Keyboard tab lands on the card (one focus target), Enter or Space triggers import modal - Pill text contrast >= 4.5:1 - Screen-reader-only labels include dataset counts - No duplicate announcements Emma Patel: timeline? If eng can pick this up today we can ship in next patch. @Josh Kim can you triage and break into two PRs: markup + CSS? Josh Kim: I'll create two branches: `feat/sample-a11y-markup` and `fix/sample-pills-contrast`. Will add unit + accessibility e2e tests. Assigning to @Sam and @Lia for review. Sam O'Neill: noted, will take the contrast PR. Lia Morales: I'll validate NVDA once markup PR is up. Also quick doc: add a small note in onboarding docs about keyboard usage of sample picker. Emma Patel: perfect. tiny nit re copy in the empty state: change "Pick a sample project to get started" -> "Choose a sample project to import and try Redwood" (makes the import intent clearer to screen reader users). Josh Kim: will change copy in `onboarding.json` and `i18n` keys. Emma Patel: cool. Let's sync in design review tomorrow 10:30. If anyone has blocking concerns post here. :thumbsup:
